nodes.text: And around them grievous mourning hovered,
as if Troy were already burning in mournful fire.
And then from the streams of broad-flowing Thermodon
came Penthesileia, clothed in the beauty of the goddesses,
both longing for grievous war
all longing for war and grim combat,
who were her handmaids, glorious though they were;
but Penthesileia far outshone them all;
as when in the broad sky among the stars the bright moon
stands out among them all, conspicuous,
in wrath at one another; and Strife guided the scales
of grievous battle, and they were no longer level;
but then godlike Memnon, beneath the base of the breast,
the son of Peleus wounded; and straight through, the black sword
leapt out; and at once his much-loved life was loosed;
not even the son of Cronus himself will defend him any longer, nor anyone else,
when he rages so and sets himself against the gods.
So he spoke, and became invisible amid the clouds;
and clothed in mist he let fly a hateful arrow,
and swiftly wounded him at the ankle; and at once pains
and my deeds, all that I did and endured for the sake of the host.
So speaking, the noble son of mighty Telamon
drove Hector’s sword through his neck; and from him the blood
gushed out rushing. And he lay stretched in the dust
like Typhon, whom the thunderbolts of Zeus burned up;
to the warlike throng of the Argives; and they, seeing [him],
all deeply pitied the far-shooting man, worn by his grievous
wound; but him, sound and free of sickness,
quicker than swift thought, made
Podalirius, equal to the heavenly gods, skilfully on top
sprinkling many drugs over the wound, and skilfully calling
the name of his father; and at once the Achaeans shouted,
all together glorifying the son of Asclepius.
And they bathed him and anointed him all over with oil
